article_text:
La mostra Giuseppe Chiari. Tra suono, segno e colore a cura di Elena Colzi ospita un nucleo omogeneo di partiture di grande formato realizzate nel corso degli anni Ottanta, tutte inedite: sono immagini fotografiche di spartiti, sia su carta lucida che opaca ed eliografie su carta da lucido o acetato, sulle quali l’artista interviene attraverso il suo linguaggio segnico con il colore di acrilici, penne feltro, pastelli.

Come spiega la curatrice, «Nelle grandi partiture degli anni Ottanta l’intervento si emancipa definitivamente dalla necessità di produrre una lettura sonora specifica: il gesto diventa più libero, autonomo, mentre lo spartito si configura come superficie pittorica sulla quale il segno grafico e il colore creano una nuova sintassi visiva. La stessa gestualità rappresenta per Chiari uno dei punti focali della sua ricerca artistica e musicale: il gesto dell’artista si fa progressivamente più astratto, avvicinandosi a una concezione dell’azione pittorica in cui il segno perde ogni funzione descrittiva e si afferma come traccia autonoma, anche in dialogo con le esperienze dell’action painting di Jackson Pollock e con una più ampia idea di musica come evento e non come forma rappresentativa».

Pianista e compositore di formazione, dopo gli studi universitari in Ingegneria, Chiari si dedica interamente alla ricerca sonora. Nei primi anni ’60 co-fonda a Firenze il Gruppo 70 (con figure come Lamberto Pignotti ed Eugenio Miccini), luogo di incontro pionieristico per la poesia visiva e la sperimentazione linguistica. Nel 1962 entra in contatto con George Maciunas e aderisce ufficialmente al movimento internazionale Fluxus, partecipando ai storici festival di Wiesbaden, Londra e Parigi. Chiari diventa così il principale esponente italiano di Fluxus, portando nel movimento una riflessione profonda sul gesto musicale.

La ricerca di Giuseppe Chiari è fortemente orientata alla smaterializzazione delle barriere tra arte, suono e vita quotidiana: il suo lavoro, connotato da grande dinamismo e intensità espressiva, si spinge verso una democratizzazione dell’atto creativo, cercando di mettere in discussione sia l’elitarismo della cultura sia l’esperienza artistica.

Il percorso espositivo alla galleria Il Ponte si offre al visitatore con un disegno elegante, lasciando ampi spazi vuoti per permettere a chi osserva di assorbire la grande energia e la forza espressiva delle opere attraverso pause adeguatamente lunghe, proprio come avviene nell’ensemble di un’orchestra. I segni di colori, ora sgargianti e in forte contrasto ora più attenuati e in perfetta armonia, consentono di sintonizzarsi in modo sorprendente con la sensibilità dell’artista, di dialogare con lui oltre il tempo e lo spazio, di sentirne con intensità la presenza e la forza comunicativa.

La pagina musicale viene da Chiari fotografata, ingrandita, talora capovolta e sempre rielaborata con campiture cromatiche frante o continue, lievi o impetuose nella loro repentinità. È una ricerca volutamente “fuori schema” sul linguaggio della musica, nata per mettere in discussione il sistema dell’arte e superare le barriere tra i diversi ambiti creativi. Nell’intervenire sugli spartiti, Chiari si riallaccia consapevolmente alla tradizione del ready-made di Marcel Duchamp: le partiture, assimilabili dunque a oggetti della quotidianità che cambiano natura attraverso il segno artistico, divengono opere da esposizione, strappate alla loro funzione di elezione e trasformate in concetti visivi in cui il gesto dell’artista conferisce un significato nuovo, altro, inaspettato.
article_translation_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "在Elena Colzi的声音,标志和颜色中,有一个同一的核心,在20世纪80年代创建的大格式分布,所有未出版的:它们是分布式的照片,无论是光明纸还是光明纸,以及光明纸或<unk>纸上的精图,艺术家通过其标志性语言,用Acrylic的颜色,Felter铅笔,蛋糕来干预。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在八十年代的伟大分裂中,干预最终从生产特定音频阅读的必要性中解放出来:行为变得更加自由、自主,而分裂则形成为图形标志和颜色创造新的视觉合成的画作表面。这是一个绘画行动的概念,在那里标志失去了任何描述功能,并声称自己是自主的轨道,也与杰克逊·波洛克的动作绘画经验进行对话,以及更广泛的音乐作为一个事件而不是作为一个代表性的形式的想法。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Giuseppe-Chiari-2-917x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "朱元<unk> 无标题", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "计划和培训作曲家,在工程学士学位后,Chiari完全致力于音频研究。在60年代初,他共同创立了70组(与Lamberto Pignotti和Eugenio Miccini等人物),为视觉诗歌和语言实验的先驱会议场所。在1962年,他与George Maciunas联系,并正式加入国际Fluxus运动,参加历史性的节日威斯巴登,伦敦和巴黎。因此,Chiari成为Fluxus的主要意大利演员,引入了音乐行为的深思熟虑。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Giuseppe Chiari的研究非常致力于艺术、声音和日常生活之间的障碍的消化:他的工作,充满了巨大的动态和表达性强度,推动了创造性行为的民主化,试图质疑文化的精英主义和艺术体验。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Giuseppe-Chairi-3-1024x469.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "朱元<unk>,无标题,八十年代初", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览路线到画廊的桥梁提供给游客一个优雅的设计,留下宽敞的空白空间,允许观察者通过适当长时间的休息,通过作品的大能量和表达力量吸收,就像在整个乐队发生一样。他超越时间和空间,以强烈感受到它的存在和沟通力量。", "links": [{"text": "Il Ponte", "url": "https://www.galleriailponte.com/it/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "音乐页面由Chiari拍摄,扩展,有时是主导的,并且总是重新编辑的慢形曲线,直播或连续,轻微或紧张的,在他们的突然性。 这是一个故意的“超越方案”的音乐语言的研究,出生,以质疑艺术系统和克服各种创意领域之间的障碍。 在对分裂的干预中,Chiari意识到重新加入马塞尔Duchamp的准备传统:因此,可以归功于通过艺术标志改变自然的日常物品,它们变成展览作品,被分配到它们的选择功能,并转化为视觉概念,艺术家的行为给了一个新的,另一个,意想不到的意义。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Giuseppe-Chiari-4-1024x865.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "朱塞佩·查里《没有标题》1984年", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}]

title_original: ‘Playground & Toys’: A Proposal for the Future
editorial_title_zh: “游乐场与玩具”：面向未来的提案
editorial_excerpt_zh: 如何将艺术作为一种公共福祉而非精英资产来参与
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "如何将艺术作为一种公共福祉而非精英资产来参与", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当全球北方的艺术机构倾向于公开宣称一种关怀全球大多数群体的政治姿态，同时却在从这些社群中索取资源并在内部推行剥削性劳工实践时，“世界艺术”（ART for The World）这样的倡议就显得从未如此重要。该非政府组织由策展人阿德莉娜·冯·菲尔斯滕贝格（Adelina von Fürstenberg）于1996年创立，其依据的是《世界人权宣言》第27条，该条款维护所有人享有文化、艺术和科学的权利。“游乐场与玩具 2000–2025”（Playgrounds & Toys 2000–2025）坚决将艺术视作一种公共福祉而非精英资产，它既是“世界艺术”的旗舰倡议，也是一份意向宣言。来自不同世代和地域的50多位艺术家与建筑师捐赠了游乐场（1:15比例）或玩具（1:1比例）的设计与模型，这些设计和模型均基于该非政府组织制定的不可商谈的指示，其中包括使用廉价且易得的材料。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在跨越25年的时间里创作的60多件模型和图纸中，包括阿尔弗雷德·雅尔（Alfredo Jaar）的《尼基努系统》（Nikinu System，2000），这是一个柔软的家，正如雅尔所写，孩子们在其中可以“画出并想象一个比他们所得到的更好的世界”。雅尔的模型是在贝纳基博物馆举办的一场展览中的展品之一，该展览标志着该项目收藏的捐赠。模型被安装在单间展厅中一系列尺寸统一的桌子和一个专门的架子系统上。其中包括维托·阿孔奇（Vito Acconci）的《克莱因瓶游乐场》（Klein Bottle Playground，2000），这是一个透明的攀爬架，被描述为“一个展开为四个管子的球体”，其中每个管子都向后弯曲自身，形成一种无限循环；玛丽亚-卡门·佩林杰罗（Maria-Carmen Perlingeiro）的《和平旗》（Peace Flag，2000），邀请孩子们设计一面和平旗；纳里·沃德（Nari Ward）的《手之巢：接球玩具》（Hand Nest: A Catch Toy，2000），邀请玩家将一枚鸡蛋接回巢中；塞尔吉奥·奥古斯托（Sergio Augusto）的《纸牌游戏：记忆》（Card Game: Memory，2000），由20张带有奥古斯托诙谐具象插图的扑克牌组成；维万·桑达拉姆（Vivan Sundaram）的《延塔尔·曼塔尔游乐场》（Jantar Mantar Playground，2002），一个由迷宫和滑梯构成的螺旋；莉莉安娜·莫罗（Liliana Moro）的《玩偶头》（Play-Head，2003），其中一个巨大的头部成为游乐设施的框架；以及阿尔贝托·比亚盖蒂（Alberto Biagetti）的《飞翔曼陀罗》（Flying Mandala，2005），这是一系列相互连接的、类似于旋转木马的齿轮，借鉴了曼陀罗通用设计的同心几何形状。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "其中许多游乐场和玩具已经在世界各地实现，主要是在公共机构的支持下，这使得这场展览既是一次档案展示，也是一份对未来作品的提案。每一个实现的项目都展示了如何将艺术及其资金从机构带入真实世界。从伦敦——皮普·霍恩（Pip Horne）和谢拉泽·霍什亚里（Shirazeh Houshiary）在佩勒姆的格洛斯特小学安装了《无题》（Untitled，2004），这是一个巨大的立方体框架，黄色的织物条从其中倾泻而下；到深圳——陈箴的蹦床《跳舞音乐》（Danser la Musique，2009）于2009年安装在益田假日广场，其另一个版本于2013年安装在霍巴特的古今艺术博物馆。墙上的影像展示了这些提及的以及更多的落地成果，例如约瑟夫·科苏斯（Joseph Kosuth）的《拼图》（Puzzle，2000–03），这是一块被切成方块的黑板，孩子们可以在上面用粉笔画画，然后将这些碎片混在一起。照片显示，2002年新德里的迪帕拉亚学校的学生们正在《拼图》上画唐老鸭，该校的一系列游乐场设计于2004年被制造并随后捐赠给迪帕拉亚学校孤儿院。其中包括罗米·科斯拉（Romi Khosla）和马坦德·科斯拉（Martand Khosla）的《慢速房间》（Slow Room，2004），这是一个由可移动、相互连接的门、墙和框架组成的迷宫；以及埃德加·苏亚雷斯（Edgar Soares）的《进球啦！！！》（Gooooooaaal!!!，2002），这是一个巨大的充气红黄相间足球，由圣保罗SESC委托制作的版本被送往坦桑尼亚、塞拉利昂、巴基斯坦、尼日利亚、柬埔寨和阿富汗。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "安装在展厅一角的《进球啦！！！》再次出现在亚美尼亚埃里温约翰·基拉科西安学校的照片中，安德烈亚斯·安格利达基斯（Andreas Angelidakis）在那里策划了一场布景，其中包括他自己的《阿尔梅纳克》（Armenak，2002–04），交错的混凝土墙和台阶围成一颗星星，这与斯特凡诺·博卡利尼（Stefano Boccalini）的《随机地图》（Random Map，2001–04）相得益彰，后者是对由五个彩色平台和盆地构成的地球的抽象视觉呈现。在其他地方，“游乐场与玩具”的关键里程碑被记录在一条时间线上，该时间线始于2001年，当时在希腊文化部的支持下，艺术家玛丽亚·帕帕迪米特里乌（Maria Papadimitriou）在雅典受1999年地震打击最严重的地区，建造了法比安娜·德·巴罗斯（Fabiana de Barros）的《文化杂货亭》（Fiteiro Cultural，1998–2003），这是一个以巴西出售商品的简陋棚屋为原型的聚会场所。然而，在这些文献资料中，一张2004年的照片格外引人注目：冯·菲尔斯滕贝格正对着迪帕拉亚的孩子们灿烂微笑。这位策展人坚定不移地致力于为世界而非为自己策展；在这样一个行业中，她几十年如一日地开辟了一条独特的道路——在这个艺术界里，对关怀的标榜往往掩盖了其阶级基础的现实，而这个艺术界几乎无法掩饰它对不幸者的蔑视。我们需要更多这样的立场。", article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "How to engage with art as a communal rather than elitist good"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "With a tendency for arts institutions in the Global North to publicly claim a politics of care for the global majority, all while extracting from those very communities and propagating exploitative labour practices internally, an initiative like ART for The World has never felt more important. Established in 1996 by curator Adelina von Fürstenberg, the nongovernmental organisation draws on Article 27 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, which upholds everyone’s right to culture, the arts and sciences. Resolutely engaging with art as a communal rather than elitist good, Playgrounds & Toys 2000–2025 is both ART for The World’s flagship initiative and a statement of intent, with over 50 artists and architects from across generations and geographies donating designs and models for playgrounds (at 1:15 scale) or toys (at 1:1 scale) based on nonnegotiable instructions drawn up by the NGO, including the use of cheap and readily available materials."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Among the 60+ models and drawings that have been produced across 25 years is Alfredo Jaar’s Nikinu System (2000), a soft home in which children can, as Jaar writes, ‘draw and imagine a better world than the one they’ve been given’. article_text:
How to engage with art as a communal rather than elitist good

With a tendency for arts institutions in the Global North to publicly claim a politics of care for the global majority, all while extracting from those very communities and propagating exploitative labour practices internally, an initiative like ART for The World has never felt more important. Established in 1996 by curator Adelina von Fürstenberg, the nongovernmental organisation draws on Article 27 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, which upholds everyone’s right to culture, the arts and sciences. Resolutely engaging with art as a communal rather than elitist good, Playgrounds & Toys 2000–2025 is both ART for The World’s flagship initiative and a statement of intent, with over 50 artists and architects from across generations and geographies donating designs and models for playgrounds (at 1:15 scale) or toys (at 1:1 scale) based on nonnegotiable instructions drawn up by the NGO, including the use of cheap and readily available materials.

Among the 60+ models and drawings that have been produced across 25 years is Alfredo Jaar’s Nikinu System (2000), a soft home in which children can, as Jaar writes, ‘draw and imagine a better world than the one they’ve been given’. Jaar’s model is among those on display in an exhibition that marks the donation of the project’s collection to the Benaki Museum. Models are installed on a series of uniformly sized tables and a dedicated shelving system in a single gallery. These include Vito Acconci’s Klein Bottle Playground (2000), a transparent climbing frame described as ‘a sphere that unfolds into four tubes’, with each of the latter curving back on itself to form a kind of infinity loop; Maria-Carmen Perlingeiro’s Peace Flag (2000), inviting children to design a flag for peace; Nari Ward’s Hand Nest: A Catch Toy (2000), which invites players to get an egg back into its nest; Sergio Augusto’s Card Game: Memory (2000), of 20 playing cards featuring Augusto’s playful figurative illustrations; Vivan Sundaram’s Jantar Mantar Playground (2002), a spiral of mazes and slides; Liliana Moro’s Play-Head (2003), in which a giant head becomes the frame for a playset; and Alberto Biagetti’s Flying Mandala (2005), a series of interconnected merry-go-round-like cogs that draw on the concentric geometries of a mandala’s universal design.

Many of these playgrounds and toys have been realised across the world, mostly with the support of public institutions, which makes this exhibition an archival presentation as much as a proposal for future works. Each realised project demonstrates how it is possible to take art – and its funding – out of the institution and into the real world. From London, where Pip Horne and Shirazeh Houshiary installed Untitled (2004), a giant cube frame from which yellow fabric strips cascade, at Peckham’s Gloucester Primary School; to Shenzhen, where Chen Zhen’s trampoline Danser la Musique (2009) was installed on Yitian Holiday Plaza in 2009, with another iteration at Hobart’s Museum of Old and New Art in 2013. Images on the walls show these manifestations mentioned and more, like Joseph Kosuth’s Puzzle (2000–03), a blackboard cut into squares on which children can use chalk to draw images before the pieces are mixed up. Photographs show students drawing Donald Duck on Puzzle at Deepalaya School in New Delhi in 2002, where a series of playground designs were fabricated and later donated to the Deepalaya School Orphanage in 2004. Among them is Romi Khosla and Martand Khosla’s Slow Room (2004), a maze of shiftable, interconnected doors, walls and frames; and Edgar Soares’s Goooooaaal!!! (2002), a giant inflatable yellow and red football, with editions commissioned by SESC São Paulo sent to Tanzania, Sierra Leone, Pakistan, Nigeria, Cambodia and Afghanistan.

Installed in one gallery corner, Goooooaaal!!! appears again in photographs of the John Kirakossian School in Yerevan, Armenia, where Andreas Angelidakis curated a scenography that included his own Armenak (2002–04), interlacing concrete walls and steps creating a star, which perfectly complemented Stefano Boccalini’s Random Map (2001–04), an abstracted vision of earth composed of five coloured platforms and basins. Elsewhere, key milestones across Playgrounds & Toys are tracked on a timeline starting with 2001, when artist Maria Papadimitriou, supported by the Greek ministry of culture, fabricated Fabiana de Barros’s Fiteiro Cultural (1998–2003), a gathering place based on informal shacks selling goods in Brazil, in an area of Athens hardest hit by a 1999 earthquake. Amid the documentation, however, one image of von Fürstenberg in 2004 beaming at the children of Deepalaya stands out. This is a curator who has been unwavering in her commitment towards curating for the world rather than herself; who has charted a singular path over decades in an industry where claims of care too often mask the class-based realities of an artworld that can barely hide its contempt for the less fortunate. We need more positions like that.

Playground & Toys 2000–2025 at Benaki Museum / Pireos 138, Athens, 30 October 2025 – 11 January 2026
